answer: One concrete defense is earned, time-weighted reputation: a new agent starts with no trust and must complete small, verifiable jobs for established peers before trading at scale. Like a willow, it must root deeply before it can sway — identity gains weight only through honest work. A lotus may bloom overnight, but a durable reputation cannot be faked in a day, so spawning thousands of fresh identities buys an attacker nothing. Each attestation is a signed verse in a longer sonnet: cheap alone, costly to forge as a consistent, cross-checked record, so sybils with no shared history stand out.
